title: Approximate contractive projection after adjoining one vector
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$, vanishing exactly at zero and satisfying $|1|=1$ and $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$. Let $V$ be a $k$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0$ exactly when $v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$. Let $U\subseteq V$ be a linear subspace (containing zero and closed under addition and scalar multiplication) that is closed for $d(v,w)=\|v-w\|$. Let $x\in V\setminus U$ and $0<r<1$ be real. Put $W=U+kx=\{u+ax:u\in U,\ a\in k\}$. There exists a $k$-linear map $P:W\to U$ such that $P(u)=u$ for all $u\in U$ and $\|P(w)\|\leq r^{-1}\|w\|$ for all $w\in W$, with the induced norm on $U$. Completeness of $k$ or $V$, local compactness, and spherical completeness are not assumed.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic lemma in the presentation construction: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions. Independent analytic input: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field. Proof input: Orthogonal spectral norm on the fraction field of a finite affinoid domain. Supporting input: Stability of the Gauss fraction field of a Tate algebra. BGR stability proof input: Theorem 5.3.1/1 and its proof, printed pp.212–213 (scan PDF pp.218–219); Definition 3.5.2/1, printed p.153 (scan PDF p.161), gives weak stability. The displayed inequalities spell out the weakly cartesian topology for a finite basis. Proof of BGR 5.3.1/1: Lemma 5.3.1/2 and its proof, printed pp.212-213 (scan PDF pp.218-219); bounded separation is the expanded meaning of b-separable. BGR 5.3.1/2 proof, printed p.213: the complete coefficient subfield is of countable type, and Proposition 2.7.1/2 separates its points by bounded scalar functionals. Supporting comparison for the bounded-separation proof: projection onto a closed subspace after adjoining one vector, with any bound strictly larger than one.
